title: StrongReject Evaluation of Standard Jailbreaks on Sub-2B Parameter Models

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong causal chain: sub-2B models are deployed on-device in sensitive settings, and documenting whether they have meaningful safety alignment directly informs deployment risk assessments. The two outcomes (no alignment or surprising robustness) both yield actionable knowledge.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Sub-2B models run easily on consumer hardware. StrongReject evaluator is open-source and automated. Standard jailbreak attacks (prefilling, adversarial suffix, role-play) have published implementations. Beginner CS students can follow existing code with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: run 3 well-defined attack types on exactly 2 small models, score with an existing automated evaluator, compare to published 7B baselines. Clear deliverable within 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: StrongREJECT and jailbreak benchmarking have been applied to 7B+ models extensively, but systematic jailbreak evaluation of sub-2B parameter models using standardized benchmarks is not well-covered. The EASE paper addresses small model alignment but not jailbreak vulnerability evaluation. This fills a gap for on-device deployment safety assessment.

evidence.source: A StrongREJECT for Empty Jailbreaks (Souly et al., 2024)
evidence.finding: Introduces StrongREJECT benchmark and fine-tunes Gemma 2B as an evaluator, but evaluates jailbreak methods on 7B+ models, not sub-2B target models.

evidence.source: Bag of Tricks: Benchmarking Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs (NeurIPS 2024)
evidence.finding: Benchmarks jailbreak attacks across multiple LLMs but focuses on 7B+ parameter models, not sub-2B models.

evidence.source: EASE: Efficient Safety Alignment for Small Language Models (arXiv 2511.06512, 2025)
evidence.finding: Proposes safety alignment for small LMs but focuses on alignment methods rather than systematically evaluating jailbreak vulnerability of sub-2B models.
